author: Rilup
headline: Non-programmer founder approved a git add -A that deleted half the website
summary: A solo non-programmer building a mobile app with Claude Code says his worst incidents came from approving changes he didn't understand, including a website wipe.
evidence: The two incidents that hurt most were the times I skipped that step and approved something without understanding it: a `git add -A` that deleted half the website, and a key-lookup bug that silently published captures without their proof for a day. Every real bug I have found came from using the app on a phone, not from reading output.

author: robblejuwaan
headline: Small company where AI agents do research, marketing, sales and engineering
summary: Agents on four Claude Max accounts run most of the company via Basecamp cards and a chief-of-staff agent; the founder mostly maintains the system itself.
evidence: We run a small company where a large team of AI agents does most of the work, not just coding: research, marketing, sales follow-up, engineering. So my answers are a bit different.

author: bshafiq
headline: Two agents politely agreeing in a loop until a massive API bill
summary: LangGraph and CrewAI agents could loop agreeing with each other overnight, so they added middleware that kills sessions after three identical messages.
evidence: if you don't wrap your handoffs tightly, you'll eventually get two agents that just politely agree with each other in an infinite loop until you wake up to a massive API bill. we ended up putting a tiny middleware layer between the nodes that hashes the payloads and kills the session if it sees the exact same message 3 times in a row. saved us a ton of money, but it feels like something that should just be built into the frameworks by now.

author: martialwave8
headline: Local voice assistant spoke hallucinated Amara.org subtitle credits aloud
summary: Their offline Whisper-Qwen-Piper voice stack turned near-silence into hallucinated subtitle credits, which the LLM then answered and Piper read out loud.
evidence: But auditing it revealed a nasty failure mode: Whisper hallucinating "Amara.org" subtitle credits on near-silence, which then gets routed to the LLM and spoken aloud by Piper.

author: takeitwhen
headline: PubMed check caught agent citations pointing at unrelated papers
summary: A 30-line script verifying every PMID against the PubMed API blocks deploys on mismatch and caught several plausible but wrong citations.
evidence: Every PMID now gets fetched from the PubMed API and the title and year are compared against what the draft claims, and a mismatch blocks the deploy. It's about 30 lines of script, and it caught several plausible-looking IDs that pointed at unrelated papers.

author: tawman
headline: Reboot broke all 45 agent seats until Claude added a symlink
summary: Running about 45 agent seats across two machines, a reboot left none able to launch due to a mise wrapper; Claude fixed it with a symlink.
evidence: Tonight a reboot left every seat unable to launch, because my `claude` was a mise wrapper that hangs in the minimal environment the orchestrator launches with. Claude fixed it with a symlink.

author: hikewatch
headline: Marketing agents sometimes invent customers or unshipped features
summary: Scheduled marketing agents occasionally fabricate customers or claim unshipped features, so they kill the run and tighten the brief.
evidence: When an agent starts inventing customers or claiming a feature that isn't shipped, I kill that run and tighten the brief.

author: mksadoughi
headline: Coordinator agent tracks tens of sessions across hundreds of millions of tokens
summary: A former multi-agent skeptic now talks by voice to one coordinator session that assigns work to role-based sessions and hasn't lost track in weeks.
evidence: What surprised me is the context. After several weeks of one agent coordinating tens of sessions, probably hundreds of millions of tokens in, it still doesn’t seem to lose track of what anyone worked on. And it takes away the headache of keeping track of who is doing what.

author: duytran7
headline: Closing the MacBook lid killed long agent turns, so they hacked pmset
summary: Ten-minute agent turns died when the laptop lid closed, so they scripted disabling sleep via Claude Code hooks and open-sourced the tool.
evidence: A 10-minute turn means you walk away, and on a MacBook walking away means closing the lid, which kills the run. caffeinate doesn't help because macOS discards IOPMAssertion on a clamshell event unless an external display and AC are both attached.

author: davidpombar
headline: Eval runs ate the rate limit their production users depended on
summary: Building an analytics agent on Azure, they learned to separate eval and production deployments after a big eval run consumed user-facing rate limits.
evidence: One thing we learned the hard way is to keep evals and production on separate deployments. Otherwise a big eval run eats the rate limit your users depend on.

author: huangrt01
headline: Spending about 1,200 dollars a month on GPT and Gemini subscriptions
summary: They pay roughly $1,200 monthly across one $500 GPT plan, three $200 GPT plans and a $100 Gemini plan.
evidence: About $1,200/month: one $500 GPT subscription, three $200 GPT subscriptions, and a $100 Gemini subscription.

author: manu69x
headline: Self-hosted models on a datacenter PS5 APU that wakes on LAN
summary: Their llama-swap server built around an AMD BC-250 sleeps and wakes on LAN, so the day's first request can take minutes.
evidence: llama-swap fronts several engines behind one endpoint so models swap on demand, on a Vulkan rig built around an AMD BC-250 (the PS5 APU sold to datacenters). The plumbing matters more than the GPU: the server sleeps (S3/S5) and wakes on LAN, so the first request of the day can spend minutes on WoL + boot + model load.
